2608.20820.title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence
2608.20820.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are vulnerable to multi-turn jailbreak attacks that progressively manipulate conversation context. Existing certified robustness methods are limited to single-turn inputs; naive multi-turn composition yields bounds that degrade exponentially in the number of turns. We introduce Multi-Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR), a framework that models conversational safety via State-Adversarial MDPs and defines $k$-turn certified robustness as the worst-case safety probability across $k$ adversarial turns. MTCR comprises: (i) compositional certification via embedding-space mode decomposition, yielding tighter certified lower bounds than naive multiplication; (ii) $(α,β)$-safety persistence, improving the degradation rate from $\underline{p}^{k}$ to $β^k$ (with $β> \underline{p}$) and yielding interpretable horizon estimates; (iii) matching information-theoretic upper bounds establishing tightness; and (iv) a unified algorithm combining these results. Experiments on six LLMs under $ε$-bounded and Crescendo-style attacks confirm that empirical safety consistently exceeds the certified bounds.
2608.20820.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）容易受到多回合越獄攻擊，這種攻擊逐步操縱對話上下文。現有的認證穩健性方法僅限於單回合輸入；幼稚的多回合組合會導致界限在回合數上指數下降。我們引入了多回合認證穩健性（MTCR），這是一個通過狀態對抗馬爾可夫決策過程（MDPs）建模對話安全性的框架，並將 $k$-回合認證穩健性定義為 $k$ 次對抗回合中的最壞情況安全概率。MTCR 包括：（i）通過嵌入空間模式分解進行組合認證，產生比幼稚乘法更緊的認證下界；（ii）$(α,β)$-安全持久性，將降級率從 $\underline{p}^{k}$ 改進到 $β^k$（其中 $β> \underline{p}$），並產生可解釋的視野估計；（iii）匹配信息理論上界以確立緊密性；以及（iv）結合這些結果的統一算法。在 $ε$-有界和 Crescendo 風格攻擊下對六個 LLM 的實驗證實，經驗安全性始終超過認證界限。
